description: The full card of one listing from its cian.ru page URL.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description:
**A Cian listing page URL, as copied from a browser or the app.** Required. Ex: `https://www.cian.ru/sale/flat/161505619/`.

Accepted: `https://www.cian.ru/{sale|rent}/{flat|suburban|commercial}//` on any cian.ru host  - 
`www.`, regional subdomains (`spb.cian.ru`, `ekb.cian.ru`, …), `m.cian.ru` or bare `cian.ru`  -  with or
without `https://`, trailing slash, tracking query (`?mlSearchSessionGuid=…`) or fragment; a coworking
place's link (`https://www.cian.ru/coworking-8404/?offerId=278651027`) too. A search-results page is
refused with a 400 pointing to `/search-by-url`; a residential-complex page to `/newbuilding`; an agent
page to `/agent`; a non-Cian host with a 400 naming the host, a non-http(s) scheme (`ftp://…`) and a
URL carrying a user name or password (`https://user:pw@www.cian.ru/…`) with a 400.

parameters.name: region_id
parameters.description:
**Region (or city) to list residential complexes in.** Optional; default `1` (Moscow).

- `1`  -  Moscow · `4593`  -  Moscow Oblast · `2`  -  Saint Petersburg
- `-1`  -  Moscow together with Moscow Oblast · `-2`  -  Saint Petersburg with Leningrad Oblast
- City-level ids work too: `4777`  -  Kazan, `4701`  -  Vladivostok.
- Take region ids from `/regions` and city ids from `/locations`; `/developer` publishes `-1` / `-2` in `regions[].region_id`.
- An id naming no region returns an empty list.
- Any other value of 0 or below is a 400.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**1-based page number.** Optional; default `1`, range `1` - `1000`.

- Pages hold `page_size` complexes; `total_pages` and `has_more` in the response tell you when to stop.
- A page past the end returns `items: []` with `has_more: false`.
- The platform serves no row beyond the 10,000th: a page reaching past it serves only the rows before it, with `has_more: false`.
- The ranking is live: if it moves while you page, a complex can repeat on the next page (and another slip to an earlier one). De-duplicate by `newbuilding_id`.
- Use `page_size=50` for the fewest page boundaries.

parameters.name: from_developer
parameters.description:
**`true` = only complexes where the developer itself sells at least one flat.** Optional.

- Keeps exactly the rows with a non-null `matching_flats_count`. Such a complex can also have resale flats by agents (see `has_agent_listings`).
- Combined with a flat filter (`with_finishing`, price, area, floor…) it becomes one condition on the SAME flat: a complex is kept only when a flat the developer itself sells matches the other filters, not when the developer sells some flat and an agent's flat matches.
- So `with_finishing=true&from_developer=true` can return fewer complexes than the two single-filter sets share.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.
- The per-room tables of developer and agent flats are on `/newbuilding` (`flats_by_rooms_developer[]`, `flats_by_rooms_agents[]`).
- Cannot be combined with `has_agent_listings=true` (a 400).

region_id.description:
**Region (or city) to list residential complexes in.** Optional; default `1` (Moscow).

- `1`  -  Moscow · `4593`  -  Moscow Oblast · `2`  -  Saint Petersburg
- `-1`  -  Moscow together with Moscow Oblast · `-2`  -  Saint Petersburg with Leningrad Oblast
- City-level ids work too: `4777`  -  Kazan, `4701`  -  Vladivostok.
- Take region ids from `/regions` and city ids from `/locations`; `/developer` publishes `-1` / `-2` in `regions[].region_id`.
- An id naming no region returns an empty list.
- Any other value of 0 or below is a 400.

page.description:
**1-based page number.** Optional; default `1`, range `1` - `1000`.

- Pages hold `page_size` complexes; `total_pages` and `has_more` in the response tell you when to stop.
- A page past the end returns `items: []` with `has_more: false`.
- The platform serves no row beyond the 10,000th: a page reaching past it serves only the rows before it, with `has_more: false`.
- The ranking is live: if it moves while you page, a complex can repeat on the next page (and another slip to an earlier one). De-duplicate by `newbuilding_id`.
- Use `page_size=50` for the fewest page boundaries.

page_size.description:
**Complexes per page, 1 - 50.** Optional; default `20`.

- Each row carries up to 5 photos, the per-room price table and the sales contacts, so a full page of 50 is a large response.
- Values outside 1 - 50 are rejected with 400.

- Send with `price_max` for a window; `price_min` greater than `price_max` is rejected with 400.
- A value above 100 billion is rejected with 400.
- Not combinable with `price_per_m2_*`.

**Lowest floor of a flat.** Optional, 1 - 200.

- Keeps complexes with at least one flat on this floor or higher.
- The row's `matching_flats_count` then counts only such developer flats.

floor_max.description:
**Highest floor of a flat.** Optional, 1 - 200.

- Keeps complexes with at least one flat on this floor or lower.
- A minimum above the maximum is rejected with 400.

not_first_floor.description:
**`true` = only flats that are not on the ground floor.** Optional.

- Keeps complexes with at least one such flat.
- The row's `matching_flats_count` then counts only such developer flats.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

floors_in_house_min.description:
**Minimum number of floors of the house a flat is in.** Optional, 1 - 200.

- Keeps complexes with a house whose storey count is at least this.
- The platform compares each house's LOWEST storey count (`houses[].floors_min` on `/newbuilding`): a sectioned 12 - 24-storey house passes `12` but not `13` or `20`.
- A complex-level test: the row's `matching_flats_count` is not narrowed by it.

floors_in_house_max.description:
**Maximum number of floors of the house a flat is in.** Optional, 1 - 200.

- Keeps complexes with a house whose storey count is at most this.
- The platform compares each house's HIGHEST storey count (`houses[].floors_max`): a 12 - 24-storey house passes `24` but not `23`.
- Complex-level: `matching_flats_count` is not narrowed.
- A minimum above the maximum is rejected with 400.

ceiling_height_min.description:
**Minimum ceiling height, in metres.** Optional, at most 10.

- Keeps complexes with a house whose ceilings are this high.
- A complex-level test: the row's `matching_flats_count` is not narrowed by it.
- The complex's range is `specs.ceiling_height_min_m` / `_max_m` on `/newbuilding`, per house `ceiling_height_m`.

ceiling_height_max.description:
**Maximum ceiling height, in metres.** Optional, at most 10.

- Keeps complexes with a house whose ceilings are at most this high.
- Complex-level, like `ceiling_height_min`.
- A minimum above the maximum is rejected with 400.

completion_years.description:
**Completion (hand-over) years, comma-separated.** Optional. Ex: `2026` or `2026,2027`.

- Keeps complexes with at least one house handed over  -  or due  -  in any of these years. Several years widen the set.
- A past year finds complexes with houses already delivered then (their `stage` reads e.g. «Сдан» or «…, есть сданные»).
- Years 2000 - 2040.

classes.description:
**Housing class, comma-separated.** Optional; several values widen the set (OR).

- `economy`  -  эконом · `comfort`  -  комфорт
- `business`  -  бизнес · `premium`  -  премиум / элит

The class of one complex is `class` / `class_key` on `/newbuilding`. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

decorations.description:
**Flat finishing on offer, comma-separated.** Optional; several values widen the set (OR).

- `without`  -  без отделки, shell & core · `rough`  -  черновая, rough finish
- `pre_fine`  -  предчистовая, white box · `fine`  -  чистовая, ready to move in
- `fine_with_furniture`  -  чистовая с мебелью, finished and furnished · `turnkey`  -  под ключ

Keeps complexes selling at least one flat with that finishing. The same values appear in `specs.decorations[].type` on `/newbuilding`.
Unknown values are rejected with 400.

promotions.description:
**Only complexes running these promotions, comma-separated.** Optional; several values widen the set (OR).

- payment: `installment_payment` (рассрочка) · `trade_in` · `maternal_capital`
- mortgage: `standard_mortgage` · `family_mortgage` (семейная) · `low_rates` · `trench_mortgage` (траншевая) · `it_mortgage` · `far_eastern_mortgage` · `military`
- discounts: `discounts_by_property` · `personal_discounts` · `subsidies_from_developers` · `gifts`

A complex's promotions are `promos[]` on `/newbuilding`, whose `type` is coarser than these values:

- `mortgage`  -  the mortgage kinds; most maternity-capital promos carry `subtype` `maternal_capital`
- `installment`  -  `installment_payment`
- `discount`  -  the discount kinds
- `bonus`  -  e.g. `gifts`, `trade_in`

Those coarse types are not filter values. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

developer_ids.description:
**Only complexes built by these developers, comma-separated developer ids (max 20).** Optional.

- Take `developer_id` from `developers[]` on a `/newbuildings` row or on `/newbuilding`. Ex: `9542`  -  Мангазея.
- Several ids widen the set (OR).
- For one developer's profile, track record and reviews call `/developer`.

metro_ids.description:
**Only complexes near these metro stations, comma-separated station ids (max 30).** Optional.

- Take `station_id` from `/metro-stations` or from any row's `metro.station_id`. Ex: `9`  -  Аэропорт.
- Several stations widen the set (OR), and they also OR with `district_ids`.

district_ids.description:
**Only complexes in these districts, comma-separated district ids (max 30).** Optional.

- Take `district_id` from `/districts` or from any row's `district.district_id` / `district.parent_id`.
- Both levels work: `23`  -  Аэропорт raion, `5`  -  САО okrug.
- Several ids (and any `metro_ids`) widen the set (OR).
- A parent district matches by the platform's own district geometry, which can leave out a sub-district a row names under it. Send the sub-district id too.

from_developer.description:
**`true` = only complexes where the developer itself sells at least one flat.** Optional.

- Keeps exactly the rows with a non-null `matching_flats_count`. Such a complex can also have resale flats by agents (see `has_agent_listings`).
- Combined with a flat filter (`with_finishing`, price, area, floor…) it becomes one condition on the SAME flat: a complex is kept only when a flat the developer itself sells matches the other filters, not when the developer sells some flat and an agent's flat matches.
- So `with_finishing=true&from_developer=true` can return fewer complexes than the two single-filter sets share.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.
- The per-room tables of developer and agent flats are on `/newbuilding` (`flats_by_rooms_developer[]`, `flats_by_rooms_agents[]`).
- Cannot be combined with `has_agent_listings=true` (a 400).

sales_start_only.description:
**`true` = only complexes that have just opened sales (старт продаж).** Optional.

- Rows in it often carry `sales_start_label`.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.
- Complexes not yet on sale (скоро в продаже) cannot be filtered.

reliable_only.description:
**`true` = only complexes carrying the platform's own «Надёжный ЖК» (reliable complex) badge.** Optional.

- The badge means at least one house under construction passed the platform's criteria: developer not bankrupt and not on the problem-developer register, a valid building permit, no more than 2 deadline shifts of up to 2 months, a full document set and a current project declaration in the state system, recent site photos.
- It is NOT the state-register (наш.дом.рф) check of `/newbuilding-reliability`, which many unbadged complexes pass.
- `/newbuilding` shows the badge in `reliable_badge` (`has_badge`, `criteria[]`, the badged `houses[]`).
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

has_video.description:
**`true` = only complexes with a video (walk-through, promo film).** Optional.

- Rows carry `has_video`; the videos are in `media.videos[]` on `/newbuilding`.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

has_viewing_booking.description:
**`true` = only complexes where a flat viewing can be booked online.** Optional.

- Rows carry `has_viewing_booking`.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction; combine with any other filter.

with_finishing.description:
**`true` = only flats sold with finishing (с отделкой  -  any finish, from white box to turnkey).** Optional.

- A flat-level filter, like `/search` `with_finishing`: keeps complexes with at least one such flat. The row's `matching_flats_count` then counts only such developer flats.
- Unlike `decorations` (the finishing types a complex offers), it tests each flat.
- For an exact per-complex answer ask `/search?newbuilding_ids=&with_finishing=true`.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

has_3d_tour.description:
**`true` = only complexes with a 3D tour.** Optional.

- Rows carry `has_3d_tour`; the filter selects exactly the rows where it is `true`.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

has_completed_houses.description:
**`true` = only complexes with at least one house already handed over (есть сданные).** Optional.

- Ready-to-move-in stock. Those rows' `stage` reads «Сдан» or «…, есть сданные»; on `/newbuilding` `is_completed` is `true` and `houses[].status` is `completed` for the delivered houses.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.
- For houses due in given years use `completion_years`.

has_agent_listings.description:
**`true` = only complexes with at least one flat resold by an agent (not by the developer).** Optional.

- The row's own figures cover the developer's listings only, so the agents' flats show on `/newbuilding` (`prices.from_agents_count`, `agents_price_min`) and flat by flat on `/search?newbuilding_ids=`.
- Cannot be combined with `from_developer=true` (a 400).
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

problem_objects.description:
**The platform's problem-object flag (проблемный объект  -  e.g. a stalled or distressed project).** Optional.

- `exclude`  -  drop problem objects
- `only`  -  list only them

The flag is `is_problem_object` on `/newbuilding`, whose `problems[]` carries the platform's warning (e.g. «Стройка заморожена!»), the problem houses and the dom.rf source.
Unset applies no restriction; unknown values are rejected with 400.

sales_leaders_only.description:
**`true` = only complexes the platform marks as sales leaders (лидеры продаж).** Optional.

- Rows carry no flag of their own for it, so this filter is the only way to see the set.
- `false` or unset applies no restriction.

parameters.name: layout_key
parameters.description:
**The layout (floor plan): its `layout_id` from `/newbuilding-layouts`, or its bare `layout_key`.** Required.
Ex: `6a452382-26be-4f5b-95b9-ab5536169c85:1` (a 1-room 41.2 m² plan in ЖК «МУЗА», `newbuilding_id` `5750446`).

- **`layout_id`** (`:`, room type `studio`, `1` - `4`, `5_plus` or `free_layout`) from
  `/newbuilding-layouts` `layouts[].layout_id` for the SAME complex  -  it always names exactly one layout.
- An `/offer` card's `newbuilding.layout_id` also works. That listing is usually among the flats returned, but
  the platform can list a flat under another layout's key (in complexes where several buildings share one
  layout catalogue); if the flat is missing, find its layout by `house_id` + `/newbuilding-layouts`, matched on
  room type and area. A complex with no layouts on `/newbuilding-layouts` (`total_layouts: 0`) can answer 404
  for a card's key.
- **Bare `layout_key`** (UUID): one key can be shared by several layouts of different room types
  (`key_is_shared: true` there); a bare shared key returns the flats of all of them together, broken down in
  `layouts_of_key[]`.
- A key the complex does not have (or whose flats have all sold) returns 404, as does a room type the key has
  no layout of.

parameters.name: price_min

- Without dates it is compared with the flat's base nightly price (`price` / `price_per_night` on the rows).
- With `check_in`/`check_out` it is compared with the stay's average price per night
  (`stay.price_per_night`), not the base price. The platform can then also list flats priced outside the
  window for the stay: every row is returned, and `in_price_window` marks it (see `price_max`).

  `3000` - `3500` is rejected with 400, as is a minimum above the maximum). Ex: `3000`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Result order.** Optional; default `default` (the platform's own relevance ranking).

- `price_asc`  -  lowest base nightly price first. With dates the order still follows the base price, not the
  stay: `stay.price_per_night` is not in order, and flats listed without a base price (`price: null`) are
  mixed in
- `newest`  -  most recently published first · `oldest`  -  oldest listings first
- `metro_walk`  -  shortest walk to the metro first (Moscow and Saint Petersburg; elsewhere rows carry no metro,
  so the order cannot be checked on them; not for `property_type=house`  -  400)

**Two-tier order.** Where a region has partner listings, each order lists the listings published on the
platform itself first, then the listings syndicated from partner booking sites (rows with `external_partner`),
in the same order on their own  -  so the order starts over where the partner block begins.

**Ties.** The order of tied listings can differ between calls, anywhere in the list where many listings tie
on the sort key, and the partner block's last pages can differ too. Read in order for one consistent
sequence.

For the most expensive flats combine `price_min` with any order. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**1-based page; 28 rows per page.** Optional; default `1`.

**How to page:** walk pages in order (1, 2, 3, …), one request at a time, and stop when `has_more` is
`false`. Reading in order gives one consistent sequence (see `sort`).

**Depth:** a query's depth is finite, drifts over time and is well below `total` for big markets; some
regional lists end far sooner than others. Past the end `items` is `[]` with `has_more: false`.

**`has_more: false`** is published only on proof of the end:

- an empty page, the platform's end marker, an empty next page or `total` reached;
- a last page that the platform repeats on every later page;
- with dates, a page of fewer than 28 flats or one whose flats all fall outside `price_min` / `price_max`
  (every row `in_price_window: false`).

**Retry signals:**

- `page_is_repeat: true`, `items: []` and `has_more: null`  -  the page could not be served this time. It is not
  proof of the end: retry the same page, or walk in order.
- `has_more: null` on a page WITH rows  -  it is not known whether another page follows.

**Timing:** pages can be requested out of order (page 1 → page 300), but a deep jump is slower than reading in
order. A jump past the end of a big list, and the last pages of a list that ends by repeating its last page, are
the slowest; allow up to about 70 s per request.

region_id.description:
**Region (or city) to search short-term rentals in.** Optional; default `1` (Moscow).

- `-1`  -  Moscow and Moscow Oblast together · `-2`  -  Saint Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast together
- city ids work too, e.g. `4777`  -  Kazan

Take region ids from `/regions` and city ids from `/locations`. An id naming no region or city returns an empty
list (`total: 0`); `0` and negative values other than `-1` / `-2` are rejected with 400.

property_type.description:
**What to rent by the night.** Optional; default `flat`.

- `flat`  -  flats and studios
- `room`  -  a single room in a shared flat
- `bed`  -  a bed in a shared room, койко-место (rare)
- `house`  -  houses and cottages

Rows say which in `category` (`dailyFlatRent`, `dailyRoomRent`, `dailyBedRent`, `dailyHouseRent`). Dates,
`/dailyrent-availability`, `/dailyrent-reviews` and `/dailyrent-listing` work for every type. Every other
filter applies to all four, except:

- `rooms`  -  `flat` only
- `room_area_min` / `room_area_max`  -  `room` and `bed` only
- `house_features`  -  `house` only
- for `house`, the flat-only filters `rooms`, `floor_min`, `floor_max`, `first_floor`, `last_floor`,
  `apartments`, `kitchen_area_min`, `balconies_min`, `bathrooms_min`, `window_view`, `amenities=loggia` and
  `sort=metro_walk` are rejected with 400.

check_in.description:
**Arrival date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.** Optional; send together with `check_out`.

- With dates the platform lists places for that stay. A row it prices for the stay gets a `stay` block with
  the stay's `total_price`, `price_per_night`, `prepayment`, `pay_at_checkin` and any discount, priced for
  `beds_min` guests; a row it lists without pricing it for the stay has `stay: null`.
- A date in the past (Moscow time) is rejected with 400, as is a stay ending after the calendar's last night
  (today + 364 days).

check_out.description:
**Departure date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.** Optional; send together with `check_in`, at least one day after it.

- Ex: `check_in=2027-03-10&check_out=2027-03-12` = 2 nights. Sending only one of the two dates is rejected
  with 400.
- For one flat's nightly calendar and an exact quote for a guest count use `/dailyrent-availability`.
- A stay that ends on the calendar's last day (today + 365) can be listed here yet refused by that quote as
  already taken.

rooms.description:
**Room count, comma-separated.** Optional; several values widen the set (OR).

- `studio`  -  студия · `1` · `2` · `3` · `4` · `5`
- `6_plus`  -  6 rooms or more · `free_layout`  -  свободная планировка

Ex: `2,3`. Only with `property_type=flat` (a room or bed search is rejected with 400). Unknown values are
rejected with 400.

price_min.description:
**Minimum price per night, in whole roubles.** Optional; `0` means no minimum.

- Without dates it is compared with the flat's base nightly price (`price` / `price_per_night` on the rows).
- With `check_in`/`check_out` it is compared with the stay's average price per night
  (`stay.price_per_night`), not the base price. The platform can then also list flats priced outside the
  window for the stay: every row is returned, and `in_price_window` marks it (see `price_max`).
- With `price_max` it forms a window that must span at least 1,000 ₽ (`3000` - `4000` is accepted,
  `3000` - `3500` is rejected with 400, as is a minimum above the maximum). Ex: `3000`.

price_max.description:
**Maximum price per night, in whole roubles, 1 or more.** Optional; `0` is rejected with 400.

- Without dates it is compared with the flat's base nightly price; with dates, with the stay's average price
  per night (`stay.price_per_night`). Ex: `5000`.
- With `price_min` the window must span at least 1,000 ₽.
- With dates the platform can also list flats priced outside the window for the stay. Every row is returned
  as served, with `in_price_window`: `false` for a row outside the window, `true` inside it, `null` when the
  row states no price to compare. Drop the `false` rows if you need the window strictly.
- A dated page whose flats ALL fall outside the window means the window's stock is used up: it answers
  `has_more: false`.

amenities.description:
**Required amenities, comma-separated  -  a flat must have ALL of them (AND).** Optional.

- `internet` · `tv` · `fridge` · `washing_machine` · `furniture` · `air_conditioner`
- `bathtub` · `shower` · `kitchen_furniture` · `dishwasher` · `loggia`

Each extra value narrows the set. Unknown values are rejected with 400. The names are those the offer card
(`/offer`) lists in `features` (`air_conditioner`, `fridge`, …; a loggia is its `loggias_count`). `loggia`
does not apply to `property_type=house` (400).

house_features.description:
**Houses only (`property_type=house`): required features, comma-separated  -  ALL of them (AND).** Optional.

- `bathhouse`  -  баня · `pool`  -  бассейн · `garage`  -  гараж

The offer card (`/offer`) lists them in `features`. Sent with another property type: 400. Unknown values are
rejected with 400.

kids_allowed.description:
**`true` = only flats where children are allowed.** Optional.

`false` or unset applies no restriction (it does not select flats that refuse children).

pets_allowed.description:
**`true` = only flats where pets are allowed.** Optional.

`false` or unset applies no restriction (it does not select flats that refuse pets).

beds_min.description:
**Minimum number of beds (sleeping places)  -  also the party size a dated stay is priced for, 1 - 30.** Optional.

- Ex: `4`. The bed count itself is on the offer card.
- There is no separate guest-count filter: with `check_in`/`check_out` every row's `stay` total is priced for
  `beds_min` guests, extra-guest fees included (without `beds_min`, for the base occupancy  -  the
  `/dailyrent-availability` quote for 1 guest).
- For one flat's maximum guests use `/dailyrent-availability` (`quote.max_guests`).

floor_min.description:
**Lowest floor the flat may be on.** Optional, −5 to 200. Ex: `10`.

Rows carry `floor`. With `floor_max` it forms a range (`3` - `5`); a minimum above the maximum is rejected with
400.

floor_max.description:
**Highest floor the flat may be on.** Optional, −5 to 200. Ex: `2`.

Rows carry `floor`; combine with `floor_min` for a range, or use `first_floor` to include or leave out the
ground floor.

first_floor.description:
**Ground-floor flats.** Optional; omit for no filter.

- `only`  -  only flats on the first (ground) floor
- `exclude`  -  leave ground-floor flats out

Rows carry `floor`. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

last_floor.description:
**Top-floor flats.** Optional; omit for no filter.

- `only`  -  only flats on the top floor of their building
- `exclude`  -  leave top-floor flats out

The two split the listing exactly. Rows carry `floor` and `floors_total`. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

apartments.description:
**Apartments (апартаменты  -  units with non-residential legal status, typical of hotel-style towers).**
Optional; omit for no filter.

- `only`  -  only apartments · `exclude`  -  only flats with residential status

The two split the listing exactly. The offer card (`/offer`) carries the listing's `is_apartment`; search rows
carry `is_apartment: true` only when their summary names an apartment, else `null`, whatever this filter. Unknown
values are rejected with 400.

area_min.description:
**Minimum total area, in whole m².** Optional. Ex: `80`.

- Flat and house rows carry it in `total_area_m2`.
- For `property_type=room` / `bed` it is the WHOLE flat's area, while their rows carry the room's own area in
  `total_area_m2`  -  filter the room with `room_area_min` / `room_area_max`.
- With `area_max` it forms a range; a minimum above the maximum is rejected with 400.
- Whole numbers only: a decimal (`40.5`) is rejected with 400.

area_max.description:
**Maximum total area, in whole m².** Optional. Ex: `30` (studios and small one-room flats).

Flat and house rows carry it in `total_area_m2`; for `room` / `bed` it is the whole flat's area (use
`room_area_max` for the room). Whole numbers only: a decimal is rejected with 400.

room_area_min.description:
**Rooms and beds only (`property_type=room` / `bed`): minimum area of the room itself, in whole m².** Optional.

- Ex: `25`. Room and bed rows carry this area in `total_area_m2`.
- With `room_area_max` it forms a range; a minimum above the maximum is rejected with 400, as is a decimal.
- Sent with `flat` or `house`: 400 (use `area_min`).

room_area_max.description:
**Rooms and beds only (`property_type=room` / `bed`): maximum area of the room itself, in whole m².** Optional.

Ex: `12`. Rows carry the room area in `total_area_m2`. A decimal is rejected with 400. Sent with `flat` or
`house`: 400 (use `area_max`).

kitchen_area_min.description:
**Minimum kitchen area, in whole m².** Optional. Ex: `10`.

- The offer card (`/offer`) carries `kitchen_area_m2`. Flats that state no kitchen area never match.
- There is no maximum kitchen-area filter.
- Whole numbers only: a decimal is rejected with 400.

balconies_min.description:
**Minimum number of balconies.** Optional, 1 - 10. Ex: `1`.

The offer card (`/offer`) carries `balconies_count`. Loggias are counted separately  -  use `amenities=loggia`.

bathrooms_min.description:
**Minimum number of bathrooms / WCs** (separate and combined together). Optional, 1 - 10. Ex: `2`.

The offer card (`/offer`) carries the counts (`combined_wcs_count`, `separate_wcs_count`).

window_view.description:
**Where the windows face.** Optional; omit for no filter.

- `yard`  -  onto the courtyard, also matching flats facing both ways
- `street`  -  onto the street, also matching both ways
- `yard_and_street`  -  both ways only

The offer card (`/offer`) carries `windows_view`. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

with_video.description:
**`true` = only flats with a video.** Optional.

Rows carry `videos[]`. `false` or unset applies no restriction.

with_layout.description:
**`true` = only flats with a floor plan among their photos.** Optional.

Rows mark plan images with `photos[].is_layout`, except where the platform marks the plan on the offer card
only (`/offer` `photos[].is_layout`). `false` or unset applies no restriction.

unique_only.description:
**`true` = only unique listings  -  drop copies of the same flat published by several hosts or agents.**
Optional.

The offer card (`/offer`) carries the listing's `is_unique`; the daily rows' own `is_unique` marker is
published as served and can differ from the card's. `false` or unset applies no restriction.

max_metro_minutes.description:
**Maximum walking time to a metro station, in minutes, 1 - 120.** Optional. Ex: `10`.

- On foot only: there is no by-transport form for daily rentals.
- In Moscow and Saint Petersburg rows carry `metro[].minutes`; for a few flats the station that qualifies is
  not the one the row shows.
- In the other metro cities (Kazan, Yekaterinburg, …) it still filters, but the rows carry no metro, so the
  walk cannot be checked on them. In a city without a metro (Sochi) nothing matches.

no_deposit.description:
**`true` = only flats without a security deposit (без залога).** Optional.

Rows then carry `deposit: null` and `terms` without «Залог». `false` or unset applies no restriction.

homeowner_only.description:
**`true` = only flats let by the owner (собственник), not by an agent or a hotel operator.** Optional.

Rows carry `is_by_homeowner: true`. `false` or unset applies no restriction.

with_photo.description:
**`true` = only flats with at least one photo.** Optional.

Almost every daily rental has photos, so this only drops the few without; rows carry `photos[]` and
`photo_count`. `false` or unset applies no restriction.

metro_ids.description:
**Only flats near these metro stations, comma-separated station ids (max 30).** Optional.

- Take `station_id` from `/metro-stations`. Ex: `9`  -  Аэропорт (Moscow).
- Several stations widen the set (OR), and they also OR with `district_ids`.
- A row's `metro[]` lists only its nearest station, which can be a neighbouring one.
- Outside Moscow and Saint Petersburg the platform links no flats to stations: a station id there selects a
  wide area around it, not the flats next to it, and rows carry no metro.

district_ids.description:
**Only flats in these districts, comma-separated district ids (max 30).** Optional.

Take `district_id` from `/districts` (a flat's own district ids are on its offer card, `/offer`; search
rows name districts without ids). Several ids (and any `metro_ids`) widen the set (OR).

sort.description:
**Result order.** Optional; default `default` (the platform's own relevance ranking).

- `price_asc`  -  lowest base nightly price first. With dates the order still follows the base price, not the
  stay: `stay.price_per_night` is not in order, and flats listed without a base price (`price: null`) are
  mixed in
- `newest`  -  most recently published first · `oldest`  -  oldest listings first
- `metro_walk`  -  shortest walk to the metro first (Moscow and Saint Petersburg; elsewhere rows carry no metro,
  so the order cannot be checked on them; not for `property_type=house`  -  400)

**Two-tier order.** Where a region has partner listings, each order lists the listings published on the
platform itself first, then the listings syndicated from partner booking sites (rows with `external_partner`),
in the same order on their own  -  so the order starts over where the partner block begins.

**Ties.** The order of tied listings can differ between calls, anywhere in the list where many listings tie
on the sort key, and the partner block's last pages can differ too. Read in order for one consistent
sequence.

For the most expensive flats combine `price_min` with any order. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

page.description:
**1-based page; 28 rows per page.** Optional; default `1`.

**How to page:** walk pages in order (1, 2, 3, …), one request at a time, and stop when `has_more` is
`false`. Reading in order gives one consistent sequence (see `sort`).

**Depth:** a query's depth is finite, drifts over time and is well below `total` for big markets; some
regional lists end far sooner than others. Past the end `items` is `[]` with `has_more: false`.

**`has_more: false`** is published only on proof of the end:

- an empty page, the platform's end marker, an empty next page or `total` reached;
- a last page that the platform repeats on every later page;
- with dates, a page of fewer than 28 flats or one whose flats all fall outside `price_min` / `price_max`
  (every row `in_price_window: false`).

**Retry signals:**

- `page_is_repeat: true`, `items: []` and `has_more: null`  -  the page could not be served this time. It is not
  proof of the end: retry the same page, or walk in order.
- `has_more: null` on a page WITH rows  -  it is not known whether another page follows.

**Timing:** pages can be requested out of order (page 1 → page 300), but a deep jump is slower than reading in
order. A jump past the end of a big list, and the last pages of a list that ends by repeating its last page, are
the slowest; allow up to about 70 s per request.
